done_when: plans/roadmap.json lists ASK-MEASURE-FILTER with its spec, the spec's Forge v1 confirmation fields record the 2026-09-17 confirmation, and forge story new ASK-MEASURE-FILTER opens the story

dismissals.because: plans/roadmap.json:274 forge story new runs against the default branch's roadmap and opens its worktree off master, so the real entry point can only be exercised once this pull request merges; the two checks it makes were run with the installed Forge in this checkout (commit d6465df, Functional check): the key matches story.KEY and is present in repo.roadmap, and records._roadmap_items reads the spec's Roadmap line with confirmed_hash equal to the body digest. Opening the story is the next step after the merge, not a repository test

findings.body: The static metadata is internally consistent, including the spec link and confirmation hash, but the patch adds no end-to-end test or recorded functional invocation proving that the real Forge entry point accepts this roadmap item and opens the story. The supplied close run only executes the repository's npm build/typecheck/tests; `package.json:16-28` contains no Forge story command, and no repository test references this key. Consequently, a roadmap/status/confirmation contract mismatch that makes `forge story new ASK-MEASURE-FILTER` refuse can still pass every reported check. Add a suite-owned test through Forge's actual command entry point and record the required functional check.
findings.title: Not done: forge story new ASK-MEASURE-FILTER opens the story

why: The measure-comparison story must continue under Forge v1: the roadmap still lists it under the old lowercase key, which forge story new does not accept, and its confirmed spec carries no Forge v1 confirmation hash
